body:
Fixed in TestAnyware 2.7.0: <https://github.com/Linkuistics/TestAnyware/releases/tag/v2.7.0>.

## Cause

The cause is not in 2.6.0 itself. It is the order of two events at the end of an `input` command.

- Since 2.5.0, the app ends a guest connection with a reset (RST) when the client leaves. This frees the descriptors at once.
- An `input` command closes straight after its last event.
- The VNC server of tart discards input that it has not yet read when a reset arrives. A pause of 10 ms before the reset keeps every event. An ordinary close (FIN) keeps every event at any time.

So the app dropped the input of every `input` command. The command still exited 0, because it had written the bytes. The measurements are in `docs/research/tart-vnc-reset-drops-input-macos-27.md`. A bare RFB client with no TestAnyware code shows the same effect.

## Change

After its last event, the RFB client of the CLI now sends a one-pixel FramebufferUpdateRequest that is not incremental, and it waits for the answer. The answer proves that tart has read the input. The app keeps the reset, so the descriptor behaviour of 2.5.0 stays.

## Checks

The checks you proposed are in the release as `task input:live`. A fixture window in a macOS 27 guest holds a text field and a scroll view taller than its window. Each check reads its effect through `agent snapshot`, never the exit status.

- `input click` focuses the field, and `input type` puts text in it.
- `input scroll` and then `input drag` of the scroll-bar thumb each move one element of the view.

All steps failed before the change and pass after it. `task input:live` passed on the release candidate and on the installed 2.7.0 on a macOS 27.0 host with a macOS 27.0.1 guest. A host-side routing test, with a fake guest that reads late and drops unread input at a reset, guards the fault. Every release now runs `task input:live`.

## Other points from your report

- Issue 2 has a different cause. Its guest crashes in the VNC server of tart, and here the guest stayed alive.
- The macOS guest versions older than 27 are removed in the same release. `vm create-golden` now accepts macOS 27 or a later major only.
- The Linux and Windows guests do not use the VNC server of tart in this way, and we did not test them for this fault.
